title: Fewer Meetings
transcript: On Monday mornings, staff at a regional insurance office used to spend an hour telling one another what they planned to do. The trouble was that several people worked on separate cases, so most updates required no response. A new manager asked employees to post brief updates before lunch on Friday and to book a meeting only when they could name a decision the group needed to make. After six weeks, the number of scheduled meetings had fallen, and staff reported having longer stretches of uninterrupted work. One team still met every morning because its members had to divide urgent claims as they arrived. The manager kept that meeting in place and asked other teams to explain what their recurring meetings helped them do.

questions.prompt: What did the manager ask employees to identify before booking a meeting?
options: A colleague who could take notes
A time when every employee was free
A case that could be closed that day
A decision the group needed to make
questions.answer: A decision the group needed to make
questions.explanation: 经理要求员工先说清楚需要集体作出什么决定。

questions.prompt: What does the manager's response to the daily claims meeting suggest?
options: Daily meetings work best when they are brief.
Urgent work should be assigned by a manager.
A recurring meeting can be worthwhile when it helps staff coordinate.
Teams that handle urgent cases should publish more updates.
questions.answer: A recurring meeting can be worthwhile when it helps staff coordinate.
questions.explanation: 理赔团队需要每天协调紧急案件的分配，因此经理保留了例会。
